Definition: to prop (literally or figuratively); reflexively, to lean upon or take hold of (in a favorable or unfavorable sense)
BiblicalUsage: Scripture uses çâmak for to prop, to lean upon, to take hold of. Across its 47 occurrences the word stays true to that sense, whether it stands in 2 Chronicles or in 2 Kings. That steadiness is what makes it worth knowing.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that çâmak proves nothing in Scripture is filler. To prop, to lean upon, to take hold of turns up again and again because God wants it noticed.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
